The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.21.1) found new features shipping in Safari Technical Preview 255 on macOS 27 which was released last week. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive.

Release notes: https://webkit.org/blog/18482/release-notes-for-safari-technology-preview-255/

New (bold) and updated keys:

  • css.properties.border-bottom-radius
  • css.properties.border-inline-end-radius
  • css.properties.border-inline-start-radius
  • css.properties.border-left-radius

  • css.properties.border-top-radius

items.content_html:
FF160 is supposed to add support for getStats() in WebTransportSendStream/ReceiveStream/SendGroup in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2021710 but Claude and tests show that it is not in, and is likely to be in 161.

This updates things to match the current state for all browsers prior to whenever this goes in.

Tests:

  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.worker.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.html?label=master&label=stable
  • https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stream-stats.https.any.worker.html?label=master&label=stable

In fact WebTransportSendStream.getStats() and WebTransportReceiveStream.getStats() always reject with NotSupportedError and WebTransportSendGroup.getStats() always resolves with an empty object. This marks the original introductions as partial.

Safari: WebTransportSendGroup.getStats() counts only datagram bytes sent through the group, not stream bytes. Marked as partial_implementation.

Chrome: add impl_url links to the Chromium tracking issues. This is expected to release around 159 - see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5235261159112704

Related FF docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46277
items.title: WebTransport stream/send group getStats(): mark partial implementations

items.content_html:
Summary

Marks ruby-position: inter-character as unsupported in Chrome and removes the inaccurate prefixed-support note. Mirrored Chromium-based entries follow the existing data model.

Test results and supporting details

  • Chromium's current parser accepts over and under and rejects inter-character. The Chrome 84 property definitions list only before and after for the prefixed property.
  • Formatting and data lint passed on an isolated older repository snapshot with the same changed file. The unit tests passed with equivalent PowerShell environment variables; npm test itself stopped on Windows because its unit-test script uses Unix environment-variable syntax.
  • I did not run browser tests.

Prepared with Codex assistance.

Related issues

Fixes #30993.
items.title: Correct Chromium inter-character ruby support

items.content_html:
Firefox 160 makes the context parameter of exportKeyingMaterial() required and adds the required outputLength parameter, matching the spec in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079306.

Firefox 155-159 implemented an earlier draft: context was optional and the output was fixed at 32 bytes.

What I've done is added a subfeature outputLength_parameter for the new parameter.

I've marked FF155-159 support as partial_implementation with a note that attempts to capture this. Note that it isn't "really" partial - it was correct (I think) at the point it was submitted. However its only been around for 5 releases so this feels a bit like a significant spec completion and hence grounds to indicate the first version as partial. Happy to remove that if you want.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46281
items.title: Firefox 160: WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial() outputLength parameter

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds compatibility data for the focus-without-user-activation Permissions Policy and notes Chromium's different default allowlist. Chrome is recorded as preview: Canary 158.0.8127.2 enabled the feature by default, while Dev 158.0.8117.2 still marked it experimental.

Test results and supporting details

  • npm test passed on the contribution branch.
  • Chrome Canary runtime configuration and Dev runtime configuration show the difference.
  • Chromium's policy definition uses an all-origins default; the HTML Standard specifies self.
  • Firefox and Safari entries follow the existing parent header data; I did not run fresh browser tests.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance.

Related issues

Fixes #30985.
